newsitem.title: USA: Cool temps slow Missouri soy, sorghum development.
newsitem.headline: Cool temps slow Missouri soy, sorghum development.

text.p: Cooler temperatures have slowed down the later stages of soybean and sorghum develpment for the week ending September 15, according to the state's Agriculture Statistics Service.
Thirty-five percent of the soybean crop is turning color, about six days ahead of last year but about four days behind the five-year average of 45 percent.
Twelve percent of the crop is dropping leaves, five days ahead of last year but three days behind the five-year average of 19 percent.

Three percent of the crop is mature compared to none last year and six percent normally. Soybean condition is rated as three percent very poor, 14 percent poor, 33 percent fair, 40 percent good and 10 percent excellent, down slightly from a week earlier.
Eighty-four percent of the sorghum crop is coloring, 12 days ahead of last year's 66 percent and three days ahead of the five-year average of 81 percent for this date.

Sixty-three percent of the corn reached maturity versus 35 percent last year and four days ahead of the five year average of 55 percent. Seventeen percent of the crop has been harvested against 15 percent last year and one day ahead of the average of 16 percent.
